answer: Erasure-coded tenure vaults: at enrollment each identity seals a shard set under its own umber salt, derived from its answer-history hash, so a clone cannot reuse a sibling's shards. Each epoch a beacon picks an unpredictable instant and demands proof-of-retrievability within ninety seconds. Time-sharing one disk across k clones fails that deadline: k identities need k machines online at once. A missed proof burns the ember escrow and resets tenure to the nadir, erasing accrued weight, so farm cost tracks simultaneous hardware, never a flat per-head fee.
